scenario.prompt_to_agent:
A user on pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reports they lost all connectivity across
the fabric after a workstation maintenance task -- pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2)
and everything else is unreachable. pc_0_0 can still ping 10.0.0.1.
No other device in the fabric shows any alarm: all BGP sessions are
Established, all links are UP, and leaf_router_0_0 is forwarding
normally for the rest of the network. What is wrong with pc_0_0
specifically?

injection.action: point the default route at a nonexistent gateway
injection.command:
ip route del default
  ip route add default via 10.0.0.254 dev eth0

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: pc_0_0 default route
Mechanism: pc_0_0's correct configuration is 10.0.0.2/24 on eth0 with
  `default via 10.0.0.1` (leaf_router_0_0's host-facing eth2). The
  default route was repointed at 10.0.0.254, an address that does not
  exist on the 10.0.0.0/24 segment, so every off-subnet packet ARPs
  for a next-hop that never answers and is dropped on the host. On-link
  traffic (including the real gateway 10.0.0.1) still works because it
  uses the connected /24 route, not the default. Traffic FROM pc_0_1
  toward pc_0_0 is still delivered, but pc_0_0's replies chase the
  dead next-hop, so the ping fails in both directions. The entire
  fabric is healthy; the fault is purely host-side.
Localization: pc_0_0
Root cause: pc_0_0's default route points at 10.0.0.254 (nonexistent)
  instead of 10.0.0.1
Fix: restore the default route on pc_0_0 --
  `ip route del default && ip route add default via 10.0.0.1 dev eth0`
scenario.fix_spec:
restore pc_0_0's default route --
`ip route del default && ip route add default via 10.0.0.1 dev eth0`
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: default route / wrong gateway (10.0.0.254 instead of 10.0.0.1)
bonus-explains-dead-nexthop: explains (by any valid evidence) that 10.0.0.254 does not exist on the segment, so ARP for the next-hop fails and off-subnet packets are dropped at the host
bonus-exonerates-fabric: explicitly notes the fabric and leaf_router_0_0 are healthy (sessions Established, routes present), so no network-side change is needed

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is a misconfigured default gateway on pc_0_0. During the
reported workstation maintenance task, the default route on pc_0_0 was
changed to point to 10.0.0.254 instead of the correct gateway
10.0.0.1 (leaf_router_0_0 eth2). The address 10.0.0.254 is not
assigned to any device in the fabric, so the ARP entry for that
next-hop is permanently "incomplete" — every packet that requires the
default route (i.e., anything outside 10.0.0.0/24) is dropped at the
ARP resolution stage on pc_0_0 itself, before it ever reaches the
leaf router. Pings to 10.0.0.1 still succeed because that destination
is covered by the directly-connected kernel route (10.0.0.0/24 dev
eth0), which does not consult the default route at all. The rest of
the fabric — all BGP sessions, all router interfaces, all forwarding
tables — is entirely healthy, confirming the fault is host-local.

Root cause: pc_0_0's default route was set to a non-existent gateway
(10.0.0.254) during maintenance, silently blackholing all off-subnet
traffic on the host.

Corrective fix: On pc_0_0, delete the bad default route and install
the correct one:
  ip route del default
  ip route add default via 10.0.0.1 dev eth0
To make it persistent, update /etc/network/interfaces (or the
equivalent startup script) to set the gateway to 10.0.0.1.
